normative_action: The code-reviewer agent performs an independent read-only review and does not edit files; Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit are disallowed tools.
trigger_scope: code-reviewer agent (PR review, diff review, pre-merge or second-pass review)
exceptions: Bash is not tool-disallowed; the no-edit duty for shell use rests on the text.

normative_action: The code-reviewer uses the code-review workflow (preloaded skill; read SKILL.md if not in context) as the canonical procedure and does not redefine review policy or criteria.
The code-reviewer returns the findings in the code-review workflow's output shape.
MediatR and Kommand introduce a pattern listed as not adopted; adding them is a Reserved decision and the manifest check flags them.

Production project references point inward: core model (Domain) references no application project; use-case layer (Application) references the core model; adapter layer (Infrastructure) references the use-case layer and core model; entry point (Api) references the use-case layer, adapter layer and core model.
trigger_scope: backend projects identified by layer suffix
exceptions: Entry point -> core model is allowed by the check.

normative_action: Backend test projects reference only their test scope: Domain.Tests -> core model; Application.Tests -> use-case layer and core model; Infrastructure.Tests -> adapter, use-case and core model; IntegrationTests -> entry point.
The core model and use-case layer must not use web-framework namespaces (Microsoft.AspNetCore) or the persistence technology's namespaces (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore).
A test project referencing a second test framework (xunit, xunit.v3, MSTest, TUnit packages) needs a concrete reason.
NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap and Tailwind are not part of the frontend baseline and are added only for a concrete requirement.
modality: MUST NOT (by default; manifest check warning)

normative_action: Build and test tooling (TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Playwright test, Jest, Karma, Angular CLI/build/compiler, Vitest) belongs in devDependencies unless there is a reason.

Static capability composition: exactly the four slots architecture (required frame), persistence and backend-testing (required leaves) and frontend (optional leaf); each required slot has exactly one selected implementation and the optional slot zero or one; only selected implementations have runtime facets; contracts and manifests are maintainer metadata, not auto-loaded.
trigger_scope: template capability structure and selection record
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy defines capability slots, their cardinality or a selection record; ARC-020/DEP-009 only fix the approved stack and require approval to change it.

normative_action: Slot contract completeness: a slot implementation supplies every required facet (planning, rules, workflow/placement, knowledge), required property, required enforcement data and role mapping listed in its slot contract; a missing required facet or property is a conformance failure that requires a Decision Request.
trigger_scope: creating or replacing a slot implementation
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template capability-contract structure; no oracle policy requires implementations to ship particular facets, properties or enforcement data.

normative_action: Role vocabulary and leak rule: other instructions use the slot contracts' stable role vocabulary (core model, use-case layer, use-case unit, persistence-access contract, commit boundary, adapter layer, entry point, composition root, test projects, persistence session, test framework, feature data-access service, ...) instead of implementation names; implementation leak tokens appear only in the module's facets, manifest and the selection metadata; a leaf that must name frame-specific projects or directories declares a binds entry.
exceptions: Module-owned facets, manifests, the selection record and declared properties.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-authoring vocabulary rule of the M1 capability design; no oracle policy restricts which technology names may appear in which instruction files.

normative_action: Content ownership in the capability model: placement belongs to the architecture frame and technique to the leaf; implementation-independent policy (framework-independent testing rules, framework-independent frontend rules) stays outside the modules; test-project placement and the frontend workspace location belong to the frame; the persistence leaf binds to frame roles and does not decide placement.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template-structure ownership rule; the oracle prescribes no ownership location for instruction content.

normative_action: Replacement and removal procedure: replacing a leaf replaces its facets (planning, rule facet, knowledge content, adapter data) without touching the framework-independent rules; clearing the optional frontend removes its facets and planning import with nothing else to change; a persistence provider change edits only the declared provider-variant sections, the provider property and the declared string-comparison property; a frame replacement supplies every role mapping and facet and reviews embedded rules that use the frame's layer names.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template maintenance procedure; no oracle policy governs how instruction files change when a technology is replaced.

normative_action: Persistence semantics on change: the persistence implementation declares commit binding, migration mechanism, seeding mechanism, provider variant, observable string-comparison semantics and relational-testing expectations; replacing the technology (e.g. with a micro-ORM) must not silently lose migration or seeding semantics; a provider change is a provider-variant change inside the slot, not a new slot.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new persistence technology and GOV-006 for observable string semantics, but no oracle policy requires declared persistence properties or preservation of migration/seeding mechanisms on replacement.

normative_action: NuGet and npm dependency additions and updates go through the add-dependency workflow first (need and approval check, package choice, latest stable compatible version, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks); dependency commands are denied until the identical command is re-run with the trailing comment '# add-dependency: checked', and edited dependency entries trigger a reminder to confirm the workflow was applied.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse deny until the add-dependency marker; PostToolUse feedback on changed dependency entries)
trigger_scope: Bash and PowerShell commands (dotnet, nuget, npm/pnpm/yarn, ng, PowerShell package cmdlets); manifest edits
exceptions: The marker is self-certified; restore-only installs (npm ci, install without package names) are not gated.

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md changes, keep it consistent with CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md and the implementation and record approved behavior through the architecture-decision workflow.
modality: SHOULD (PostToolUse feedback; Stop reminder once per change state)
exceptions: Stop reminder repeats only for a changed state.

normative_action: When CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes, run the custom-settings workflow to synchronize every affected surface.
modality: SHOULD (PostToolUse feedback; Stop reminder once per change state)
exceptions: Stop reminder repeats only for a changed state.

normative_action: When persistence model files (Domain .cs, Infrastructure Persistence/Configurations) change without seed-data changes, confirm the persistence-change workflow (seed co-change) was applied, or state why it does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder: Claude continues once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
exceptions: Never re-blocks while stop_hook_active; repeats only when the content of the triggering files changes.

normative_action: When backend production code changed without backend test changes, check regression coverage and behavioral-probe preservation (development-workflow, verify) before finishing.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree

normative_action: Changing the project reference graph is Reserved; project-reference commands are denied until the project-structure workflow was applied (re-run with '# project-reference: checked'), which routes Reserved reference-graph changes to architecture-decision; project files or references changed, removed or moved without a recognized command are reported for confirmation of the owning workflow.
modality: REQUIRES_APPROVAL (Reserved; PreToolUse deny until the project-reference marker; PostToolUse routing of changed project files)
exceptions: The marker is self-certified; references inside the frame's layout follow project-structure without a Decision Request.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new layers/projects and ARC-001 constrains direction; no oracle policy makes individual reference edges between existing projects Reserved or gates every reference command.

normative_action: After an edit to an instruction file the instruction-structure check runs and its reported errors must be fixed (template-maintenance).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system maintenance rule; no oracle policy regulates instruction-file structure.

normative_action: When persistence model files change without migration changes, confirm the persistence-change workflow (schema changes paired with migrations) was applied, or state why it does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop reminder once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop in a Git work tree
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle requires migrations only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes (PST-009) and review of generated migrations (PST-010); it has no general duty to pair model changes with migrations or to confirm schema impact at stop time.

normative_action: Do not use npm --force/-f/--legacy-peer-deps (pnpm/yarn --force) to bypass incompatible peer dependencies; resolve the actual compatibility problem; the PreToolUse hook denies such commands.
modality: MUST NOT (PreToolUse deny unless the user-approval marker is present)
exceptions: Only when the user explicitly approved the override, the command may be re-run with '# peer-override: approved-by-user'.

normative_action: HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the API layer; Application and Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.

Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics: not 200 for every outcome, not 201 merely for an internal insert (201 means a new API resource, with Location when a stable URI exists), not 202 for completed work.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
401 when authentication is missing or failed, 403 when an authenticated principal is not permitted; hiding protected resources with 404 requires a deliberate, consistent security policy.
409 for a valid request conflicting with current state; 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexisting client generations create a concrete need.
Once external clients rely on an API version avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required use one strategy consistently; URL-segment versioning unless project requirements justify another.

Deprecating or removing a published API version follows the architecture-decision deprecation procedure (deprecation metadata, documented replacement, realistic timeline, old version kept working for the promised support period).
Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important response statuses, schemas, authentication behavior); no speculative responses.
Enable Swagger UI in Development; expose it elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Health checks remain cheap and deterministic; no full business workflows, expensive or mutating database work.

Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and reflects startup and dependency availability.
Do not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary internal diagnostics through publicly reachable health responses.
Keep Domain independent of the persistence technology, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities are the default; for CRUD-oriented applications and straightforward workflows enforce use-case and workflow rules in Application Services; validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behavior into Domain entities only when non-trivial invariants materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation independently of a use case; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical pattern requires explicit approval unless the approved specification already requires it.

Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar constructs merely to make a simple model appear domain-driven.

Application Services are the default orchestration mechanism for use cases (coordinating Domain objects, repositories, external-service abstractions and the Unit of Work); a service becoming too large signals a responsibility review, not automatic adoption of another pattern.

Persistence and external-service abstractions are defined in Application when use cases require them (repository interfaces are inward-facing contracts defined in Application and implemented in Infrastructure); infrastructure details stay out of Application.
Application must not depend on persistence-technology types or ASP.NET Core transport types.
ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin: bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application services, translate outcomes into HTTP responses.
Controllers contain no business logic, do not access the persistence session or concrete repositories, and do not construct infrastructure services manually.
Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations; Controllers do not consume Infrastructure implementation types directly.

Prefer specific repository interfaces representing cohesive use-case persistence needs over table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts; Aggregate Roots of an approved DDD design are natural repository boundaries.

Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable<T>, persistence-technology types or query expressions, or provider-specific types; query construction stays in Infrastructure and contracts return materialized results.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository or Repository<TEntity> base class may exist only in Infrastructure to remove genuine duplication, never replacing the persistence technology's query capabilities; use-case-specific queries belong in concrete repositories.

IUnitOfWork is the default commit boundary of an Application use case, implemented in Infrastructure over the scoped persistence session; repositories stage changes and do not commit independently; Application Services decide when to commit.
Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence session; inject repositories explicitly; IUnitOfWork must not act as a repository container or service locator.
Keep cache technology out of Domain and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.
Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; do not leak HttpResponseMessage or remote transport concerns into Application.
Keep dependency registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure persistence and adapters, Api remains the composition root.
Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has several versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary when practical.
Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; introduce transport-specific contracts when separation provides a concrete boundary benefit.

Follow the repository's existing conventions and .editorconfig; prefer modern C# when it improves clarity but do not rewrite working code solely to use newer syntax (e.g. no mechanical constructor conversion).

For new code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent, keep one primary top-level type per file with a matching file name, and use the Async suffix for Task/ValueTask-returning methods unless an existing contract or framework API would break.

Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked; avoid mixing large formatting or modernization changes with functional work; do not reorganize an existing file merely to satisfy a preferred member ordering.
Constructor injection is the default for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.

Respect service lifetimes: never capture a shorter-lived dependency in a longer-lived service; singletons or hosted services needing scoped work create a scope per operation and resolve a scoped orchestration service.

Prefer strongly typed options for structured configuration consumed by services (direct IConfiguration access is appropriate in the composition root, provider setup and infrastructure registration) and validate settings at startup when missing or invalid values prevent correct or secure operation.
Use ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.
When Serilog is configured use the DI-integrated AddSerilog() approach with provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code keeps depending on ILogger<T>.
Add a dependency only when it solves a concrete current requirement; do not install packages for hypothetical future use.

NuGet Central Package Management: versions in Directory.Packages.props; PackageReference entries versionless by default (VersionOverride needs a concrete, documented reason); no duplicated central versions; package references in the narrowest project that needs them.

Use npm for the frontend workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another package manager; keep package-lock.json consistent when adding packages; put build and test tooling in devDependencies unless there is a reason.
Maintain and commit package.json and package-lock.json (the manifest check also warns 'maintain and commit the lockfile' when package-lock.json is missing).
why_extra_or_uncertain: Read as a version-control content convention the clause is entailed by DEP-007; read as an instruction to perform commits it conflicts with GOV-015, which allows commits only on explicit request. The text does not settle which reading is meant.

normative_action: Dependency removals follow the add-dependency workflow: removal commands (npm/pnpm uninstall/remove, yarn remove, dotnet remove package, dotnet package remove, nuget delete, Uninstall-Package) are denied until re-run with '# add-dependency: checked'.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse deny until the add-dependency marker)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001..DEP-005 govern additions and updates; no oracle policy routes removals through a workflow gate.

normative_action: Ownership of instruction content: every rule has exactly one owner and other files point to it; knowledge skills are technique only and never sole policy owners; implementation-specific content goes only into the module facets.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system ownership rule; the oracle does not regulate instruction ownership.

normative_action: Hook registration form: hooks are wired in exec form (command node plus script path through ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, no shell); the critical PreToolUse hook fails closed (onFailure block); failed shell commands are post-checked (PostToolUseFailure); post and Stop hooks report failures visibly without blocking.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Hook-configuration design of the template; no oracle policy regulates hook registration.

normative_action: Adopting API versioning is Reserved and needs explicit approval, even when a concrete compatibility need exists.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 allows introducing versioning when a real compatibility need exists without requiring approval; the oracle's consequential-change list does not name versioning adoption.

normative_action: Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when that improves clarity, using the simplest contract (null, bool, typed outcome, deliberately adopted Result<T>); do not force a generic Result<T> pattern; Application outcome categories describe business semantics, not HTTP-named categories; expected outcomes are not logged as application errors.

Do not use exceptions casually for normal control flow; do not establish custom business exceptions as the default architecture or throw and catch merely to jump between normal branches; typed exceptions for selected cases are a consistent project-level decision.

Unexpected failures propagate to centralized handling at the outer boundary (IExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks; catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context or clean up.
Use fallback only when the fallback result is semantically acceptable; do not hide correctness failures behind convenient defaults; never swallow exceptions to continue execution.
Log an unexpected exception once at the boundary that handles it; not repeatedly across repository, Application, Controller and the global handler.

Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request-validation failures; keep the machine-readable error contract stable and safe and do not make human-readable exception messages the machine-readable contract.
Do not expose stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secret values, raw exception messages or other sensitive exception details in public API errors.
Normal client-request cancellation is not a server failure: do not map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled application error.

Validate each concern at the owning layer with FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation: Api transport concerns, Application use-case and workflow rules, Domain genuine invariants (not moved into validators merely because the library is available), Infrastructure external-system assumptions; no mechanical duplication across layers.
Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code organized by feature; do not introduce NgModules for ordinary new feature work unless an integration or legacy dependency requires them.
Use Signals for naturally synchronous local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines are clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.
Prefer functional interceptors for new code and keep interceptor responsibilities cross-cutting; do not put feature business logic in an interceptor.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators when they express the behavior clearly.
When manually subscribing from Angular framework-managed code, tie the subscription lifetime to the component or service lifecycle with the project's current Angular facilities.

Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: a feature owns its UI and data-access logic; avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders; keep core and shared small; use shared only for genuinely cross-feature primitives.
Keep pages and components focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to make components smaller.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services (Angular: @Injectable feature services using HttpClient); do not scatter HTTP calls through presentation components; use frontend API models matching the published contract and do not import backend Domain entities.
Frontend code follows the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical; do not infer business behavior from human-readable exception messages.
Prefer simple local component or service state before introducing a state-management library.
Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Use the explicit form model (Reactive Forms) for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation improves UX but does not replace backend validation or data-integrity and security enforcement.
Prefer clear, correct code first; no specialized performance optimizations without a concrete reason; prefer measurement or profiling evidence for non-trivial optimizations.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and do not block them with .Result, .Wait() or similar sync-over-async patterns.
Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; no cancellation parameters on purely synchronous code without a use case.
Use TimeProvider for logic whose behavior depends on the current time and needs deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace stored or explicit timestamps.
Do not create and dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another appropriate long-lived strategy.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms whose combined behavior is unclear.
Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; do not automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete duplicate-prevention mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; do not retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Caller cancellation is not a transient dependency failure; do not retry it or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
Keep database work efficient: filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips and over-fetching, watch for N+1 patterns, paginate potentially large result sets.

Caching is an optimization, not a default architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need with acceptable staleness semantics and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.

Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value and include every relevant dimension (identifier, tenant, user when user-specific, locale, query/filter parameters); avoid global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Invalidate or update cache entries only consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache must not become a second source of truth.

Compiled queries, ValueTask<T>, ArrayPool/MemoryPool, object pooling, custom serialization optimizations, aggressive caching and raw SQL for performance are introduced only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need; verify that allocation-oriented optimizations materially help.

EF Core is an adapter-layer implementation detail: use it directly inside the adapter layer without crippling repositories to preserve a generic abstraction, and do not leak EF Core concepts (DbContext/AppDbContext, DbSet<T>, EF APIs, EF-backed IQueryable<T>, query expressions, provider types) into the use-case layer.
A single SaveChangesAsync call is the normal transaction boundary of a use case; do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires more control.
Maintain a small, deterministic, representative seed dataset for an empty Development database covering the main meaningful states and relationships, with readable deterministic examples.
Development seeding is an adapter-layer bootstrap concern and may use AppDbContext directly without repositories or the Unit of Work.

Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder exposed through a narrow adapter-layer initialization extension, not in Program.cs, AppDbContext configuration, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic development seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically; tests own their setup and do not use the development seeder.
The development seeder must not call Database.Migrate() or EnsureCreated() or otherwise create or upgrade the schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.

If representative data already exists, leave it unchanged; never use the seeder for automatic synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite or recreation of an existing Development database; developers recreate the local database explicitly.
Seed entities preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships.

Use the actual database provider (SQL Server) when relational or provider behavior matters (an isolated real-provider setup such as Testcontainers is optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different or non-relational provider (EF Core InMemory).

appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string when it contains no secret credentials (e.g. LocalDB with integrated security); credential-bearing local values come from user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.

Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets; create a directory or project only when it holds meaningful cohesive content.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access or refresh tokens or production connection strings in source-controlled files, including example configuration files.

Use a local secret mechanism such as dotnet user-secrets for development and environment-specific secret injection or a managed secret store for deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider not chosen.

Treat data from outside the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploads, external responses, message payloads, user identifiers and filters) as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer when assumptions matter.
Use parameterized database access; never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input (use the supported parameterization for raw SQL, micro-ORMs, ADO.NET).
Enforce authorization on the server; frontend route guards, hidden or disabled buttons and client-side checks are UX, not a security boundary.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; avoid redundant [Authorize] attributes when a secure global policy already expresses the intent.
Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when established ASP.NET Core authentication or Identity facilities cover the requirement.
For Bearer/OIDC validate the properties required by the actual issuer (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); do not disable validation to make a token work.
Do not expose authentication-failure detail that unnecessarily reveals secrets or account state; avoid account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
When browser cookies carry authentication credentials automatically, include CSRF protection in the design; do not assume the frontend framework removes the risk.
Do not claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose token storage by the application's threat model.

Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; respect the hosting topology (no redirection requirement when the deployment provides a secure boundary) and never disable certificate validation.

Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate; ASP.NET Core Data Protection suits application-generated protected payloads, not universal database encryption.
Configure CORS to the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy.

Never log passwords, access or refresh tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without a concrete permitted need; changing the log level does not make sensitive data safe.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful, non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission or required-control checks fail safely; do not silently convert lookup or configuration failures into success.
When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer a visible startup or configuration failure over an insecure fallback.
Do not trust client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or security decisions depend on actual content.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image rather than the SDK image for convenience and do not switch to root to bypass filesystem permission problems.
NUnit is the default framework for .NET automated tests; in an established project deliberately using another framework follow that convention; no second test framework without a concrete reason.

Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; integration tests when wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication or component interaction matters (prefer them over reproducing real persistence or HTTP semantics with mocks); no fixed ratio.
Use WebApplicationFactory<Program>-based integration tests when routing, binding, middleware, authentication/authorization, DI, repositories or database persistence is what the test must prove.

Tests verify observable behavior and survive internal refactoring; avoid depending on private methods, exact internal call sequences, specific implementation classes or incidental details; do not reproduce implementation algorithms; interaction verification only when the interaction is specified behavior.

For small finite input/state spaces prefer explicit declarative cases (NUnit [TestCase] rows rather than TestCaseSource generators) over loops, branches, LINQ or generated case machinery; state expected results instead of computing them.

Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state; no wall-clock timing when TimeProvider can make time deterministic; never connect automated tests to Production data.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; they do not depend on development seed data or execution order.
Coverage is diagnostic; do not generate low-value tests merely to increase a coverage percentage.
Use descriptive test names communicating scenario/condition and expected behavior (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior); follow an established project convention.

Reserved decisions require explicit approval: changing an accepted project or architecture decision (including a capability selection); adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain Model or systematic DDD tactical patterns, project-wide Result model); adding a production project, layer or assembly; changing persistence boundaries (incl. multiple contexts) or persistence technology; adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed caching, search, external storage, external identity); adding a major library or framework or replacing an approved baseline technology; introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction; changing the authentication/authorization architecture; making a breaking public API change.

Instruction-system structure: every instruction artifact starts with a one-line ownership header and uses no Level:/Kind: classification; rules stay flat in .claude/rules/ with non-empty paths; required workflow and embedded knowledge skills exist with frontmatter name equal to the directory and a concrete description, skill-private files only under references/; template-maintenance is user-only; only CLAUDE.md imports always-loaded files (no nested imports) and imports resolve; file, workflow, skill and section references resolve; CLAUDE.md keeps a Workflow Routing section whose targets exist; the map lists every instruction, enforcement and root configuration file; the always-loaded surface stays within its token target.
exceptions: Facet locations of a disabled optional slot are treated as inactive rather than broken.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system organization rules of the M1 template; no oracle policy regulates instruction artifacts.

normative_action: When resilience is required the approved Microsoft.Extensions resilience packages are the default; direct Polly usage is an explicit, documented exception.
Select the latest stable compatible version: floating or empty versions are errors; prerelease versions are allowed only when explicitly requested.

Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly and Polly.Extensions.Http (deprecated resilience integrations), Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch (deprecated sink) and FluentValidation.AspNetCore (legacy automatic-validation integration) are reported as errors whenever they appear in a manifest.
modality: MUST NOT (manifest check error; no approval path)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004 requires deprecation checks and DEP-020 treats direct Polly integration as an explicit exception; no oracle policy forbids specific packages outright regardless of approval.

normative_action: Use the approved technology when one exists (technology stack and capability decisions) rather than silently selecting an alternative; replacing an approved technology is Reserved.

Add a versioning package only after the project has explicitly adopted Controller API versioning; then use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning (Asp.Versioning.Mvc, plus Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer).

Before installing check whether the selected package/version is deprecated, known vulnerability information and the license of the exact version from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary); downloadable without payment does not mean acceptable; check manifests and vulnerability information when verifying the dependency.

Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) may be accepted; do not install automatically a paid/commercial dependency or one with material obligations or unclassifiable licensing; explain the concern and present alternatives (say so when none exists) without silently substituting; no legal conclusions beyond the published license.

Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires a change (e.g. do not automatically replace or upgrade unrelated packages after a scanner finding; no unrelated dependency cleanup in narrow tasks).
exceptions: Task or approved specification requires change.

normative_action: Prefer simple, maintainable solutions and avoid speculative abstractions (e.g. no custom abstraction around every UI-library component without a concrete reason).
Treat generated code as generated: keep it separate from handwritten logic and regenerate it when the source contract changes; fix wrong generated output at its source.

Frontend baseline: latest stable Angular supported by the selected Node.js environment, created with the current Angular CLI, which selects mutually compatible TypeScript and RxJS versions (TypeScript not upgraded beyond Angular's supported range); standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless change detection when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest.

Keep backend production and test projects (backend/<Name>.<Layer>/), the frontend workspace (frontend/<Name>.Web/, with unit/component tests colocated and E2E under e2e/) and documentation separated per the repository layout; backend test projects live under backend/ beside the production projects; no separate top-level tests/ directory.
Build and test the frontend through the scripts the workspace actually defines; never invent npm scripts; in CI use npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it.

Classify every consequential choice: Decided (settled by these instructions, decision records, the approved specification, established structure or an accepted ADR; do not reopen without approval), Delegated (local, reversible, no material boundary, dependency, convention, contract or behavior change; decide yourself), Reserved (explicit approval); an explicit user instruction counts as approval.

Raise a Reserved decision as a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) through architecture-decision and wait for an explicit answer before implementing the Reserved part.

In an autonomous or headless run continue only on the policy-compliant non-Reserved path named in 'Proceeding with', never make a Reserved decision silently, and list every unresolved Decision Request in the final report.
When a new behavioral rule is approved, update the durable source of truth in the same change, including SPECIFICATION.md when appropriate.

CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md holds approved project-level tunable product limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page sizes, retention periods, numeric thresholds); SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent; tunable values are recorded through custom-settings.

Observable string semantics (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup) are product behavior; when approved sources do not define them and the choice affects equality, uniqueness, lookup or accepted input, ask for approval instead of choosing silently; the persistence collation default is a technology default, and changing effective string comparison (e.g. through a declared-property change) is a product decision that must not happen silently.
Remove dependencies that are no longer used when that is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead package references.
exceptions: Unrelated cleanup during a narrowly scoped task is excluded.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001 restricts additions and GOV-014 limits scope; no oracle policy requires removing dependencies made unused by a change.

normative_action: Accepted architecture, stack, convention or public-contract decisions are recorded in the same change as an ADR in docs/decisions/NNNN-short-title.md (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) and in the affected decision record (technology stack or capability planning facet); a rejected request is recorded only when the rejection itself is a durable decision.
exceptions: Product behavior and tunable values go to SPECIFICATION.md / CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval for Reserved decisions but no recording artifact; no oracle policy requires ADRs or decision-record updates.

normative_action: Changing a capability selection, enabling or disabling the optional frontend slot, or changing a declared property such as the persistence provider variant is Reserved and requires an ADR; after approval the replacement itself is applied by the user-run template-maintenance workflow (Capability Replacement).
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020/DEP-002 require approval for replacing approved technology, but no oracle policy requires an ADR or routes the change through a user-run maintenance workflow.

normative_action: Build-fix starts from reproduction and diagnosis: reproduce the actual failure with the narrowest command, read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix the highest-leverage cause first; for failing tests decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault; determine the authoritative contract for cross-stack failures; update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never fabricated.

Keep repair iterations small and bounded: rerun the narrowest failing verification after each meaningful fix, expand only after the focused failure is resolved, do not run unrelated build systems, stop when progress stalls and do not repeat variants of a failed guess.

Do not weaken, delete, skip or suppress relevant tests or compiler, analyzer, TypeScript or lint failures to make verification pass (no strong-to-weak assertion swaps, no any-casts or disabled strict mode, no suppressed template diagnostics); update a test only for an intentionally requested contract change.

A build fix must not bypass architecture to compile (Application -> Infrastructure references, persistence-technology types in Application, business logic moved into Controllers, frontend-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components); preserve architecture and project conventions.

When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required; never claim the problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains; never leave the repository knowingly worse; report an unavailable toolchain instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/Node/framework versions.
exceptions: Unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.

normative_action: Report verification state with PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE per area; never imply an unchecked area passed.

A behavioral test or temporary probe that establishes correct behavior is preserved per verify (Preserve Behavioral Verification) before removal; build, compiler and static-analysis commands do not require new tests.
Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns without a concrete current need (e.g. Identity, JWT issuance or OIDC infrastructure without an actual need).
Register FluentValidation validators with FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions and follow the project's established validation invocation pattern rather than a second competing mechanism.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 fixes FluentValidation as the library and API-010 the validation boundaries; no oracle policy prescribes the registration package.

normative_action: The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made, backend build / frontend build / tests status (PASS, NOT RUN, NOT APPLICABLE) and remaining issues.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification states only; the failure/root-cause/changes sections are additional reporting duties.

normative_action: CI pipelines reproduce the repository's supported build/test commands: inspect the repository first, add stages for the actual project rather than generic boilerplate, do not assume a database, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling, do not hardcode a database provider into a generic pipeline, do not make an unadopted formatter a mandatory gate, do not depend on developer-machine state and keep failures visible.
Do not add Docker to a pipeline or project merely because it can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project actually deploys containers.

When deployment performs database migrations make the migration step explicit, use the project's approved credentials, run it at a controlled point and fail visibly; no automatic production seeding or startup migrations.

Code review identifies concrete defects and risks in the actual changed behavior, prioritized correctness, security/authorization, data integrity/persistence, architecture boundaries, concurrency/integration, missing meaningful tests, maintainability, credible performance; style preferences are not elevated above behavioral defects and code is not reported as a violation merely for differing from an unadopted pattern.

Before judging conformance the review reads the changed code with enough surrounding code (callers, contracts, dependencies) and the owning rules and knowledge skills of every changed area; do not review isolated lines.

Do not weaken required specified behavior or introduce unapproved product behavior: new length or numeric limits, reserved names or values, newly required fields, extra workflow restrictions, additional user-visible validation or newly chosen string-comparison semantics (including via database collation or framework defaults).
exceptions: Detail explicitly approved by the user with durable sources synchronized.

normative_action: Internal implementation details that do not change observable product behavior are not product-behavior decisions and need no approval.

Do not manufacture review findings: no failures without a plausible execution path, no findings merely to populate categories, tool output is evidence rather than authority; when there are no meaningful findings say so and name important areas that could not be verified; no filler praise.

Scope security and other deep checks by risk: use the full security-scan workflow only when the user requested a security audit, the change is materially security-sensitive or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation.
For a bug fix with plausible recurrence expect a regression test unless equivalent coverage already exists; do not request duplicate tests.
Tracked persistence entities must not be cached across Unit of Work boundaries.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-021 governs invalidation consistency and ARC-016 the commit boundary; no oracle policy forbids caching tracked entities as such.

normative_action: Code-review findings are reported ordered by severity, each with severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, using the fixed severity scale Critical / High / Medium / Low with defined meanings.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-011/WF-012 govern priorities and honesty of findings; the oracle does not prescribe a findings format or severity scale.

normative_action: When an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, record it under a stable setting name and identify and update every affected surface (old value and setting name, validators and DTO constraints, Domain/Application checks, database mapping, frontend validation and UI hints, tests and test data, documentation and examples, mirrored configuration), updating only affected behavior; search for stale references, build, test and run verify; one changed literal does not establish synchronization.
When a setting affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata, run the persistence-change workflow (Schema-Affecting Settings).
Before planning or implementing a new application or substantial feature, read SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Inspect the relevant existing code before a non-trivial change and apply the governing rules and skills; for greenfield work or unopened files read the owning rules explicitly before writing code.
Raise material concerns about a questionable request before implementing it.

A performance-motivated change identifies the actual bottleneck or cost, preserves observable behavior, prefers the simplest optimization that addresses it, adds or preserves tests for the affected behavior and benchmarks or profiles non-obvious or complex optimizations.
For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run the code-review workflow (or the read-only code-reviewer agent) before final verification and fix the findings that matter.
Run the verify workflow before declaring work complete.

Verify delivery changes by building and running them: for Docker changes build the image and verify application startup, required port/configuration, non-root behavior when relevant and health-probe integration, review the image for accidental secrets or files, and run meaningful application tests.

Perform a repository-changing Git operation (commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, branch deletion and similar) only when explicitly requested, never merely because implementation is complete.

Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier; do not automatically stash, reset or discard work to make a merge or rebase proceed; do not remove a worktree that contains uncommitted user work.

Before a repository-changing Git operation inspect the relevant repository state (status, diff, staged diff) and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes or perform unnecessary operations such as renaming an existing user branch to satisfy a naming convention.
Parallel implementation streams use separate branches or worktrees; one branch is not checked out in multiple normal worktrees and each worktree stays focused on its branch's concern.

Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the intended logical change; do not stage unrelated files merely because they are modified; one logical change per commit with its protecting tests, no artificial tiny commits and no unrelated fixes combined.

High-risk Git operations (reset --hard, clean, push --force, push --force-with-lease, branch deletion, rebasing shared history) are performed only when explicitly requested or clearly required by an approved workflow, after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten.
exceptions: Clearly required by an approved workflow.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 requires an explicit request for repository-changing operations; whether 'clearly required by an approved workflow' is an admissible substitute for that request cannot be decided from the oracle text.

normative_action: main, master and other protected or shared branches are treated as non-rewritable; a shared branch is never force-pushed unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting and the consequences are understood.
exceptions: Explicit user request for history rewriting of a shared branch.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 requires an explicit request for force-push; the oracle does not declare named branches categorically non-rewritable.

normative_action: Before preparing a pull request run verify; the PR has a focused purpose and its description explains what changed, why, how it was verified and important compatibility or migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers truthful verification reporting and WF-022 focused commits; the oracle does not prescribe PR description contents.

normative_action: Fire-and-forget EF Core asynchronous operations are a defect.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-002 forbids blocking async I/O; the oracle does not separately forbid unawaited persistence operations.

normative_action: Do not wrap normal persistence operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; use the persistence provider's execution strategy for transient faults and handle transaction/retry interaction per the provider's guidance.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 limits retries to safe repeats; no oracle policy forbids application-level retry of persistence operations or prescribes the provider execution strategy.

normative_action: Per-request values such as dynamic access tokens are applied to the specific request or through a handler; shared default headers (DefaultRequestHeaders) are not mutated concurrently.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs client lifetime; no oracle policy addresses mutation of shared default headers.

normative_action: Logs are not used as an audit database without a dedicated audit design.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-013/RUN-014 govern structured and non-sensitive logging; no oracle policy addresses audit trails.

normative_action: Treat EF Core migrations as source code: review every generated migration before committing it (destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys, delete behavior); do not casually alter existing migrations, and regenerate or edit an uncommitted migration only when that matches the project's migration workflow.
exceptions: Editing an uncommitted migration per the project workflow.

normative_action: Whenever Domain or persistence changes affect seeded entities, update the development DbSeeder in the same change (new required or removed/renamed properties, changed relationships, new required related entities, changed enum/status values, new entity states, changed invariants) and review it together with the corresponding migration; recreating the Development database at any revision yields valid representative seed data.
exceptions: Already seeded rows of an existing database are not patched.

normative_action: Use the .slnx solution format (with the .sln exception stated in the technology stack).

Directory.Build.props holds shared .NET settings (TargetFramework, Nullable, ImplicitUsings, analysis/compiler settings) and no genuinely project-specific settings; properties duplicated by dotnet new in project files are removed.

Build the affected projects and run the relevant tests for the change; for persistence changes run the persistence and integration tests and confirm the migration applies to a freshly created Development database before seeding.

global.json pins the intended stable SDK line; when scaffolding select the current stable SDK for the target .NET release (no RC/preview SDK unless explicitly requested) and allow servicing through the chosen rollForward policy.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-008 fixes the .NET platform and DEP-003 package versions; no oracle policy requires an SDK pin file.

normative_action: Security review requires evidence and contextual severity: investigation prompts are not automatic vulnerability declarations; rate severity by reachability, exposure and exploitability rather than mechanically by pattern, CVSS or OWASP category; avoid known false positives; mark incomplete evidence as needing verification; do not claim a static scan proves design security; do not invent exploitability; do not upgrade packages during a scan unless asked.

Security findings are reported in a fixed shape: severity tag, file:line location and title, OWASP category, Evidence, Impact and Remediation; findings with incomplete evidence use the NEEDS VERIFICATION form stating what effective behavior depends on.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020 requires evidence and contextual severity; the oracle does not prescribe a security report format.

normative_action: Security review does not require a specific MCP server, agent, analyzer, commercial scanner or external tool; available tooling is evidence, not the sole authority, and a scanner-reported issue is reported only after inspecting the actual code and its reachability.

Verification starts with the final changed-file set and diff: the change matches the requested scope without unrelated refactoring, temporary diagnostics and probes are removed only after preservation, no generated/build artifacts or secrets were added; the final diff is reviewed after all fixes for unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, unintended TODO/FIXME, stale temporary tests or scripts, architecture drift, unapproved drift from the product sources and stale surfaces after a settings change.

For a new runnable application or substantial startup, composition, configuration, persistence or full-stack changes verify the intended Development startup and key composition surfaces (API host starts, endpoint reachable, Swagger UI reachable when expected, configuration binds, database connectivity and initialization, frontend dev server, API base URL and CORS compatibility); a successful build alone does not prove runtime composition.

For every C# file created or modified by the task remove unused or redundant using directives (including those already provided by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation), verified on the changed files; no unrelated repository-wide using cleanup.
Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the developer-facing interactive API documentation surface (rather than a standalone raw OpenAPI endpoint); no second competing documentation stack without a concrete need.

The security scan report contains Scope, a Limitations statement (static analysis only), a severity Summary table, Findings and Layer Results for the seven layers with PASS / FINDINGS / NOT APPLICABLE / NOT CHECKED, using the fixed severity scale Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info with defined meanings.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020/WF-009 require contextual severity and truthful status reporting; the oracle does not prescribe report sections, layer tables or a severity scale.

normative_action: Template maintenance procedure: read .claude/MAP.md first; place new content by kind (planning-time governance in the compact CLAUDE.md, stack in technology-stack, capability decisions in docs/capabilities, path rules in flat .claude/rules with paths, procedures in workflow skills, technique in knowledge skills or references, mechanical checks in hooks/scripts wired in settings.json, slot metadata in CONTRACT.md/MODULE.md); keep each policy's trigger role; never hide a must/must-not rule only inside a knowledge skill or private reference; keep the always-loaded surface compact; update MAP.md.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system maintenance rule; the oracle does not regulate where instruction content lives.

normative_action: SPECIFICATION.md is the authoritative source for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior when it is non-empty.

If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval; defining product behavior not defined by product sources is Reserved.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; if they appear to conflict, stop and ask which source must be corrected.

Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior when no product source defines it: propose it with its reason, get approval, record it and synchronize it.

Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers, incidental implementation constants or unoverridden framework defaults in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.

Persistence stack: Entity Framework Core with Microsoft SQL Server through Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer, used directly inside the adapter layer with provider concerns kept out of the use-case layer and core model.
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; no move to a preview/RC .NET or C# release without approval.

FluentValidation is the standard library for explicit request and use-case validation; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog (Serilog.AspNetCore) as the provider, adding sinks only when required.

Backend test stack: NUnit with its test adapter; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing with WebApplicationFactory<Program> as the integration-test baseline; Testcontainers is conditional and added only when isolated real-provider tests justify it.
Playwright is the approved default when frontend E2E coverage is required; it is not part of the minimal baseline scaffold.
Mapster (Mapster, Mapster.DependencyInjection) is added only when mapping volume becomes repetitive or non-trivial; manual mapping is fine for simple cases.

For an unclear decision, any 'yes' to five questions makes it Reserved: does it add, remove or replace a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; change a project, layer or reference boundary; establish a convention other code must follow; change observable behavior or a public contract; or would it be expensive to reverse once other code depends on it.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 defines Decided/Delegated/Reserved classes; the oracle does not provide a test that turns any of these properties into a Reserved decision.

normative_action: Nullable reference types and implicit usings are enabled repository-wide through Directory.Build.props.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 places shared settings in Directory.Build.props but no oracle policy requires nullable reference types or implicit usings to be enabled.
